reports.title: CHOICE HOTELS INTERNATIONAL REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: The Company is updating certain aspects of its full-year 2026 outlook. The outlook includes forward-looking non-GAAP measures used by management to assess expected performance. Adjusted metrics exclude the net surplus or deficit from reimbursable activities related to franchised and managed properties, due diligence and transition costs, and other items. The outlook includes Harvest Hosts’ operating results from the October 1, 2026, acquisition date and reflects the impact of the Company’s two recent hotel dispositions, except as otherwise noted.

Full-Year 2026 | Prior Outlook
Net income | $178 to $185 million | $230 to $241 million
Diluted EPS | $3.92 to $4.07 | $5.07 to $5.31
Adjusted net income | $315 to $322 million | $312 to $323 million
Adjusted EBITDA | $641 to $651 million | $635 to $650 million
Adjusted SG&A growth, excluding Harvest Hosts | Approximately 9% | Mid-single digits
Adjusted diluted EPS | $6.92 to $7.07 | $6.86 to $7.10
Effective tax rate | 26% | 26%
Full-Year 2026 vs. 2025 | Prior Outlook
Global RevPAR growth | 1.5% to 2.5% | 0% to 1%
U.S. RevPAR growth | 1.5% to 2.5% | 0% to 1.25%
U.S. royalty rate growth | Approximately 9 bps | 7 bps to 9 bps
Global net system rooms growth | Approximately 1.5% | Approximately 1.5%

The net income guidance range has been lowered from the Company's prior outlook primarily to reflect higher expected marketing and reservation system reimbursable expenses, driven by increased investment in franchisee-facing tools and guest delivery capabilities. The revision also reflects a $24 million charge related to the termination of an arrangement that included an option to acquire a European hospitality business, $6 million in non-cash impairment charges related to owned hotels, lower expected equity in earnings of affiliates, and higher interest expense.

The adjusted net income guidance range has been narrowed from the Company's prior outlook to reflect higher expected adjusted EBITDA, higher interest expense, and lower expected equity in earnings of affiliates.

The Company raised the midpoint of its adjusted EBITDA guidance range, primarily reflecting stronger global RevPAR, higher U.S. royalty rate expansion, and an estimated $1 million net benefit from the Harvest Host acquisition and two recent hotel dispositions, partially offset by higher adjusted SG&A expenses. The revised adjusted SG&A outlook, excluding Harvest Host, reflects primarily non-recurring spending on certain strategic initiatives and artificial intelligence-enabled capabilities, as well as higher accounts receivable reserves.
